question: Does one shared causal encoder, trained on the training splits of many openly licensed neural, EMG, motion and force datasets at once, forecast movement for people, animals and sessions that no NeuroTranslation fit has used better than matched controls (persistence, linear trend, ridge, the frozen NeuroTranslate 0.0 encoder, a random encoder of the same architecture and the best single-source encoder), with the same adapter budget? Secondary: at a matched number of unique training windows, do more sources help more than more data from one source?
claim_limits: Results cover the listed datasets, tasks, inputs and horizons only. Each primary human set has 10 people; E3 has one animal and carries no population claim.

Forecasts are made on archived recordings. Published marker trajectories were filtered or gap-filled by their authors and AJILE12 pose is an offline estimate, so no statement about live latency follows.
Surface and intramuscular EMG record muscle electrical activity; they are not nerve recordings. EEG and ECoG are field potentials. Spike counts come from sorted units in public archives.

Measured, derived (for example DeepLabCut pose, OpenSim joint angles, mean-absolute-value EMG envelopes, author-filtered EEG) and simulated values are labelled apart in every file, token and report. No simulated data enter the primary mixture.

A win or a loss holds against the listed controls at the stated adapter budgets. It is not evidence of general biological translation, and the quantity-versus-diversity result holds only at the data scale tested (W_max windows).
People, animals, sites, recordings, tasks, windows and events are counted separately (MIXTURE-MANIFEST.json).

qualification_gate.applies_to: every dataset or part of one before it enters the mixture; results recorded in MIXTURE-MANIFEST.json before the freeze
qualification_gate.Q1_licence: CC0, CC BY, ODC-By, MIT, CDLA-Permissive or PDDL, checked on the deposit page at P2 with the sha256 of the licence text recorded. No share-alike data in public weights; non-commercial data may give scores only. Never the worm imaging deposit (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.19388374) or the SLEAP sample recordings.
qualification_gate.Q2_role: Only units with a frozen training role in an existing protocol (fit, train, development, engineering) or never-assigned units sent to training by a published hash rule. Excluded: every validation, assessment, confirmation, final, test, held or reserved unit, every consumed evaluation group, and every unit of a line that is in flight or on hold.
qualification_gate.Q3_access: Local, or reachable by per-file or byte-range reads that never decompress a reserved member.
qualification_gate.Q4_clock: Streams count as paired only if they share one file with one clock or a documented synchronisation that passes a check on training units. Otherwise they enter as separate acquisitions and are never paired within one window.
qualification_gate.Q5_labels: Units and modality recorded per channel; every value labelled measured, derived or simulated. EMG is never labelled as a nerve recording.
qualification_gate.Q6_causality: Any author filtering (forward-backward, gap filling, zero-phase high-pass) is recorded. Features we compute use only samples at or before the end of each 20 ms step.

allocation.script: allocate.py (Python standard library only; reads no recording)
allocation.check: python3 allocate.py --check ALLOCATION.json (add --gait120-tail TAIL to recompute the E1 member list from the public last 262,144 bytes of figshare file 53167640)
allocation.inner_fold_rule: rank the training units of a dataset by ascending sha256('pooled-encoder-0.2|fold|' + dataset + '|' + unit); fold = rank mod 5; fold 0 is inner validation. Datasets with fewer than 3 independent units use 5 equal time blocks per recording, the latest block being inner validation.

inner_validation_units.sabes: latest time block of each recording

allocation.d_arm_rule: for k in {2,4,8} and draw in {0,1,2}: order candidate sources by ascending sha256('pooled-encoder-0.2|D|k' + k + '|draw' + draw + '|' + dataset); the arm uses the first k sources in that order that are eligible (at least W_max/8 inner-training windows, counted at P2)
allocation.E2_sessions: calibration session 3, scoring session 4 for every participant
allocation.E2_window_rule: for k = 0, 1, 2, ...: candidate issue frame = int(sha256('pooled-encoder-0.2|ajile12|' + participant + '|ses-' + session + '|' + k), 16) mod n_frames; accept if eligible (protocol section 7.2) and at least 2 s from every accepted issue time; stop at 600 accepted or k = 200000
allocation.E4_rule: rank labs by ascending sha256('pooled-encoder-0.2|ibl-bwm-2023_12|lab|' + lab); after the IBL audit, the first 3 labs in this order with at least 4 never-referenced mice are evaluation labs; never-referenced mice of every other lab may enter training
allocation.adapter_folds_E1: E1 adapter penalty folds: rank the 66 Gait120 development people by ascending sha256('pooled-encoder-0.2|adapter-fold|gait120|' + unit); fold = rank mod 5
computed_later_by_fixed_rules: W_max and the eligible D-arm sources (P2, from MIXTURE-MANIFEST.json)
folds of FALCON M1 days and IBL training mice if admitted
E2 issue frames (after the freeze, from the session files)

representation.clock: 20 ms causal steps; step k covers [20k, 20k + 20) ms of the recording and becomes available at its end; every feature uses samples inside or before the step
group_slots: kin (markers, keypoints, joint angles, IMU, hand or cursor)

features.spikes: count per unit per step (raw counts, not normalised)
features.field: per channel, causal log band power over the trailing window (100 ms or 200 ms, chosen by inner folds) in 4-8, 8-13, 13-30 and 70-150 Hz (the last band masked where the sampling rate is below 400 Hz), plus the last value of a causal 10 Hz low-pass
features.emg: log RMS of the raw signal within the step after a causal 20 Hz high-pass; datasets that ship only an envelope (Katmah) give the envelope value at the step end, labelled derived
features.kin: last sample in the step and its change from the previous step; positions relative to the window anchor at the last input step (mean of pelvis markers for full-body marker sets, mean of the shoulders for upper-body keypoints, the point itself for single hand or cursor trackers); joint angles and IMU as recorded; the vertical axis mapped to +Z by a per-dataset axis map

channel_identity.readin: for a group with channels c, read-in matrix W[c] = E(c) P with rank 32, applied to x and to gelu(x), plus a presence term, then LayerNorm
shared_vocabularies: anatomical markers and keypoints (Plug-in-Gait names mapped to landmark names)
channel_identity.per_recording_rows: spike units, ECoG electrodes, HD-EMG electrodes and unmapped EMG channels get learned rows; a coordinate MLP adds electrode position where it exists (MNI, grid row and column, array position)

representation.normalisation: per-channel z-score with statistics from training units only (inner-training units for model choice, all training units for the final model); spikes stay raw counts; evaluation sets use their adaptation data for statistics
representation.context_token: learned embeddings of dataset, species, task, body plan and a measured / derived / simulated flag; the dataset id is replaced by an 'unknown dataset' id with probability 0.1 during training so that unseen datasets have a trained token
representation.masks: absent groups and channels are key-masked
representation.augmentation: with probability 0.2 a 3D marker window is replaced by a random orthographic 2D projection (azimuth uniform 0-360 degrees, elevation uniform -20 to +40 degrees) of its upper-body and leg landmarks, flagged derived
representation.window_unit_for_counting: non-overlapping 1.2 s segments per recording; training crops may overlap

architecture.fusion: one transformer layer over the group tokens of each step (absent groups masked; groups dropped in training become a learned mask token); the step token is the mean of the present group tokens
architecture.core: pre-LayerNorm causal transformer with rotary position embedding (RoPE), GELU feed-forward of 4 x width
core_arms: hybrid: transformer plus a GRU state token carried between windows
architecture.heads: for each group and horizon, a linear map to 32 dimensions dotted with an output identity row per channel; spikes output a log rate

XXL.condition: runs only if XL beats L by at least 1% relative on the selection score

architecture.short_segments: segments shorter than the context are left-padded and masked (Gait120 steps last 1.5-1.65 s; ds003739 sessions 10 min)

objective.spikes: Poisson negative log-likelihood of counts; h = 1 is next-neuron prediction
objective.continuous: Huber loss (delta 1.0) on the change from the latest value, in normalised units
objective.group_dropout: each present group is dropped from the input with p = 0.25 (at least one measured group kept) and stays a target; dropped groups are also reconstructed at h = 0
objective.loss_normalisation: each group's loss is divided by its baseline loss on the training mixture (persistence for continuous groups, per-unit mean rate for spikes); groups and horizons are averaged with equal weight
objective.dataset_sampler: p_d proportional to N_d ** tau, N_d = number of individuals of dataset d; tau in {0, 0.5, 1} chosen on leave-one-dataset-out folds; no dataset above 25% of examples (excess redistributed proportionally)
objective.within_dataset_sampling: individuals uniform; recordings in proportion to duration; crop start uniform over valid starts

optimiser.name: AdamW
optimiser.weight_decay_on: matrices only (not LayerNorm, biases or identity rows)

training.schedule: linear warmup over 2% of updates, cosine decay to 10% of peak
training.batch: 128 windows x T steps (32,768 step-tokens at T = 256)
training.pass_definition: one pass = a number of step-tokens equal to the unique 20 ms steps of the training mixture in use
training.data_order: per dataset, window list ordered by sha256('pooled-encoder-0.2|order|' + seed + '|' + dataset + '|' + window_id); sampler draws from counters keyed by sha256 of (seed, update, slot); sampler state saved in every checkpoint
determinism: math scaled-dot-product attention kernel on the GPU
training.records: LOCK (source, array and script sha256) -> ATTEMPT (argv) -> FP32 safetensors checkpoint with optimiser and sampler state -> reload-equality check -> RESULT (sha256, wall time, peak RSS and GPU memory, threads, versions) -> READBACK
training.threads: at most 16 threads in total, pinned within CPUs 16-31; the GPU is shared with other workflows' browser tests, which have priority
training.software: own virtual environment under the private track folder; ROCm torch read-only use permitted; versions recorded in every RESULT

model_selection.principle: every choice uses folds inside the training units only (ALLOCATION.json inner_folds); no evaluation byte is read before the freeze
model_selection.inner_validation: fold 0 of each dataset (fold 4, the latest time block, for time-block datasets); the inner-training units are the rest
model_selection.selection_score: for each dataset, the mean over its present groups of (model loss / baseline loss) on its inner-validation units, with identity rows for new units fitted on the first 50% of each inner-validation recording and the score taken on the last 50%; the selection score is the mean over datasets with equal weight; lower is better
model_selection.lodo_score: for each wave-1 dataset left out of training: adapter fitted on its inner-training units, score on its inner-validation units; mean over datasets
order_of_choices: tau in {0, 0.5, 1}: leave-one-dataset-out at size M, transformer, T = 256, seed 20261127, budget 2 passes
size and passes: ladder XS, S, M, L, XL with the chosen tau, up to 40 passes, checkpoint every 2 passes; the (size, pass) with the lowest selection score
core: transformer, GRU and hybrid at M and L; a non-transformer core is used only if it beats the transformer by at least 1% relative at both sizes
context: T in {64, 128, 256, 512} and field window in {100, 200} ms at size M
XXL: run only if XL beats L by at least 1% relative; chosen only if it then has the lowest selection score
model_selection.ties: within 0.5% relative, the smaller or simpler option
model_selection.final_runs: chosen configuration trained on all training units for the chosen number of passes, 3 seeds

precision.tier_1: CPU FP32 deterministic: reference for all issuing and scoring
precision.tier_2: GPU FP32 with math attention: reference training route up to M (L if time allows)
precision.tier_3: GPU BF16 autocast with FP32 master weights and optimiser: ladder, arms and XL and above
precision.bf16_acceptance: matched full runs of S and M, BF16 with 3 seeds and GPU FP32 with seed 20261127, same data order: BF16 is accepted if the selection score and the inner-validation readout metrics differ by at most max(1% relative, the spread across the 3 BF16 seeds); otherwise the final runs use GPU FP32
precision.issuing: every reported forecast is issued in FP32 on the CPU from an FP32 export with a fixed batch shape of 32; arms of the quantity-versus-diversity study may be issued on the GPU in FP32 with fixed padded shapes and a CPU spot check of 1,000 windows (maximum absolute difference reported)
precision.run_to_run: one quantity arm is repeated with identical settings and the parameter and metric differences are reported

adapters.channel_map: each evaluation channel is mapped onto the shared vocabularies where its name allows
adapters.identity_rows: rows for unnamed channels (units, electrodes) trained for 500 AdamW updates at learning rate 3e-3 with the encoder frozen, using the forecasting heads
adapters.readout: ridge regression on the frozen issue-step features, penalty chosen from {1e-3, 1e-2, 1e-1, 1, 10, 100, 1000} by the folds of each set's adaptation units
adapters.secondary_arm: LoRA rank 8, 200 updates, predeclared and reported separately
adapters.release_format: NumPy-only FP32 reader; each readout in its own file recording the parent encoder sha256

E1.units: Gait120 S001-S010 (10 people), left out of the chair-rise roster because they lack source-aligned plate data; archive file 53167640 never fetched by any earlier study
E1.files: 1,198 members (TRC, OpenSim joint-angle MOT, RawData.mat), 759,080,170 compressed bytes, listed with CRC-32 in ALLOCATION.json (member list sha256 c80220bc1ddca0e08f6912409afc61060f5841c5136b0034e003f626d5663ecb)

E1.eligibility: all 12 target markers finite at the last input frame and at both target frames; applied identically to every method
E1.not_scored: LevelWalking Trial01 of each person (EMG scaling trial) and static trials
E1.aggregation: windows -> step -> trial -> task (7 tasks, equal weight) -> person
E1.sensitivity: E1 without the steps of the 23 S010 members listed in state_at_writing
E1.note: markers are author-filtered, so past inputs may carry a little future information; this affects every method alike and the result is labelled archive-only

E2.label: unseen dataset, unseen people
E2.units: AJILE12 participants 03-12 (DANDI 000055, version 0.220127.0436); owner option: keep 08-12 back and score 03-07
E2.files: calibration = session 3, scoring = session 4 for every participant (asset ids, bytes and sha256 in ALLOCATION.json); other sessions never opened; access by ranged HDF5 reads of the pose series and, for the secondary input, the ECoG of the needed windows only
E2.adaptation: adapters and ridge fitted on the pooled calibration sessions; penalties by leave-one-participant-out over calibration sessions; ECoG identity rows per participant from that participant's calibration session
E2.windows_primary: hash-drawn issue frames (ALLOCATION.json E2 window_rule), 600 per session
E2.windows_secondary: native ReachEvents onsets of the scoring session under the earlier next-person selection rule
E2.eligibility: issue at least 512 steps (10.24 s) after the session start; the 15 prior frames have finite shoulders and finite wrist, elbow and shoulder of both arms; shoulder frame passes w >= 1 pixel, |mean(d)| >= 0.5 w and |vertical component of the perpendicular| >= 0.10; both wrists finite at frames j+7 and j+14
E2.inputs_primary: past pose (wrists, elbows, shoulders, ears, nose), 30 Hz resampled to 20 ms steps by the last sample in each step, expressed in the shoulder frame built from the 15 prior frames only and divided by the shoulder width
E2.inputs_secondary: pose plus ECoG band power, compared with ECoG taken 60 s earlier
E2.targets: contralateral and ipsilateral wrist displacement from the last prior frame to 8 and 15 frames later (0.267 s and 0.500 s), shoulder-normalised units; contralateral side from the session's native ReachEvents description and the published implant hemisphere
E2.primary_metric: mean over the 2 wrists and 2 horizons of the 2D Euclidean error, shoulder widths (normalised image units)
E2.note: pose is DeepLabCut output (derived) from a separate model per participant; the published unit conversion is undefined, so no millimetre values are reported

E3.label: unseen sessions of one animal; Jenkins is unseen by 0.2 but seen by earlier NeuroTranslation fits
E3.files: MC_Maze full (DANDI 000128, 2009-09-25) and MC_Maze Large (DANDI 000138, 2009-10-06) training files (sha256 in ALLOCATION.json); desc-test files never opened
E3.adaptation: per session: identity rows for units and ridge on the NLB 'train' trials; penalties by 5 trial folds
E3.issue_times: every 50 ms from 250 ms after the trial start while the +100 ms target lies inside the trial
E3.inputs_primary: past spikes (at least 200 ms, up to the chosen context) and past hand position
E3.primary_metric: Euclidean error, mm, windows -> trial -> session, sessions equally weighted
E3.secondary_metric: next-step spike log-likelihood in bits per spike against a per-unit mean rate
E3.uncertainty: trial bootstrap stratified by session; no population claim

E4.role: primary only if IBL is admitted before the freeze; otherwise not run
E4.label: new labs and mice; a seen dataset if IBL training mice enter the mixture
E4.units: the first 3 eligible labs in the ALLOCATION.json E4 lab order, earliest Probe00 session of each never-referenced mouse
E4.adaptation: per session, adapters on the first 60% of trials in time order
E4.targets: wheel angle change at +100 ms, rad, from past wheel, task events and spikes
E4.primary_metric: absolute error, rad, windows -> trial -> mouse

secondary_sets.B1: Gait120 validation 22 and confirmation 22 people, never-opened tasks LevelWalking, SlopeAscent, SlopeDescent, StairAscent and StairDescent, E1 targets; labelled 'people already used in another study's evaluation, new tasks'; runs only with owner approval
secondary_sets.A4: Camargo et al. lower-limb biomechanics as a whole held-out dataset; needs protocol version 2 after a person-overlap check against 10.35090/gatech/70296 and a licence check; nothing is fixed here
secondary_sets.seen_dataset_arm: optional: 0.2 continued on AJILE12 sub-01 session 3 only and scored on E2 only, to measure what seeing the dataset adds; run if GPU time allows and reported whatever the result
secondary_sets.published_task_refits: the published 0.0 tasks refitted on 0.2 with the same adapters, reported only as a development comparison on previously used people

evaluation.not_used: E5 (no group offered by the walking-scale allocation) and W-track ZT2 (closed)

controls.persistence: zero change from the last value

linear_trend.E1: least-squares line over the last 100 ms (10 frames) of each target marker
linear_trend.E2: endpoint velocity of the 15 prior frames (last minus first, scaled by 8/14 or 15/14)
linear_trend.E3: least-squares line over the last 100 ms of hand position
linear_trend.E4: least-squares line over the last 100 ms of wheel angle

controls.ridge: ridge on the per-step input features of the last 16 steps (320 ms), target = change from the last value, penalty grid and folds as the adapters
controls.frozen_0.0: movement-weights.npz encoder frozen; a 4-token adapter maps each 80 ms chunk of the last 16 steps to the 6 encoder inputs and is trained with a linear head for 500 AdamW updates at 3e-3; the head is then replaced by the ridge readout on the final-token features; joint_alpha is not used
controls.random_encoder: 0.2 architecture at the final size, initialised with seed 20261127, never trained; same adapters
controls.scrambled_0.2: every weight tensor of 0.2 (seed 20261127) with its entries permuted by a fixed permutation (seed 20261128); same adapters
controls.single_source: size-M encoders for every wave-1 source with the arm budget (screen); the best by selection score and the nearest source per set (E1 Gait120, E2 Ofner, E3 Sabes, E4 IBL training mice) are retrained at the final 0.2 size and token budget on all their training units, seed 20261127, keeping the checkpoint with the best score on their own source's inner validation
controls.scratch_size_S: a size-S model trained from random initialisation on the set's adaptation data only, 2,000 AdamW updates at 5e-4, batch 32 windows, then the ridge readout
controls.matched_history: frozen 0.0 with its 4-token adapter over the last 16 steps (320 ms), and 0.2 scored on the same 320 ms history

task_specialists_H3.E1: chair-rise attention recipe refitted on the 66 development people with E1 targets
task_specialists_H3.E2: next-person pose ridge recipe, penalty 1, fitted on the calibration sessions
task_specialists_H3.E3: NeuroTranslate 0.1 eight-pass neural-maze model refitted on the session's train trials

controls.wrong_pairing: for every neural or EMG input: the same model with that input taken from another time (E1 EMG from the previous step of the same trial; E2 ECoG 60 s earlier; E3 spikes from the next val trial, wrapping)

metrics.weighting: within an individual, windows are averaged, then trials (or segments), then tasks; each person or animal then has equal weight
metrics.relative_error: R_i = error_i(model) / error_i(persistence) per individual; set mean of R_i reported with the physical error
metrics.composite: mean over the scored primary sets (E1, E2 and E4 if run) of the set mean R; E3 is reported separately
metrics.seeds: 0.2 and every 3-seed control are scored per seed and each individual's error is averaged over seeds; no ensembling

uncertainty.method: paired bootstrap over individuals (people or mice)
also_reported: range when one individual is left out
uncertainty.composite: individuals resampled independently within each set

success_rules.set_pass: 0.2 passes a set if, for every control in {persistence, linear trend, ridge, frozen 0.0, random encoder, fold-chosen best single source}, the mean paired difference (0.2 minus control) is below 0 with the bootstrap 95% upper bound below 0, and at least ceil(0.7 n) of the n individuals have a lower 0.2 error than that control (7 of 10; 4 of 5 under the owner option)
success_rules.H1: E2 passes, and E1 passes or (if IBL is admitted) E4 passes. An intersection-union test, so no multiplicity adjustment. Each set is reported separately.
success_rules.H2: composite R of the D_all arm at W_max minus the mean composite R of the Q arms at W_max is below 0 with the bootstrap 95% upper bound below 0
success_rules.H3: per set, 0.2 against the task specialist with the set_pass criteria; reported per set, no overall claim
success_rules.floors: a human set is scored only if at least 8 of 10 people (4 of 5) have at least 50 eligible windows; otherwise it is reported as insufficient and counts as not passed
success_rules.reporting: every predeclared result is published, wins and losses alike; if H1 fails the result is stated as no evidence that the pooled encoder improves forecasts for new people over the listed controls

quantity_diversity.model: size M transformer, chosen tau and context, crops of 60 steps aligned to the counted windows, batch 128
quantity_diversity.budget: U = 40 x W_max / 128 updates for every arm (same steps x batch); effective passes reported
quantity_diversity.W_max: the smallest number of unique inner-training windows in any Q anchor, rounded down to a power of 2 (computed at P2)
quantity_diversity.Q_arms: anchors Gait120, ds003739, Ofner and W-track (IBL training mice replace W-track if admitted); levels W_max/16, W_max/4, W_max
quantity_diversity.D_arms: k in {2, 4, 8} sources, 3 hash-ordered draws each, from sources with at least W_max/8 inner-training windows; each source gives W_max/k windows; D_all uses every eligible source
quantity_diversity.P_arms: Gait120 with 3, 13 or 52 inner-training people and ds003739 with 2, 4 or 14, at W_P windows
quantity_diversity.sealed_prediction: before any W_max run, a power law through the inner-validation selection scores of the W_max/16 and W_max/4 levels of each Q anchor predicts its W_max score; the prediction file is hashed and its sha256 recorded before the W_max runs start
quantity_diversity.scoring: every arm is scored on the inner-validation units (in distribution) before the freeze and on E1, E2 (and E4 if run) after it, with the standard adapters

leak_checks: subject-identifier disjointness between every training list and every evaluation list
file-hash disjointness and content-hash de-duplication across derived caches and original files (for example area2 against Dryad)
download timestamps of every evaluation file after the freeze commit
no evaluation file path appears in any LOCK file before the freeze
